body: What can I say, I run an RSS feed reader. I fetch millions of URLs a day. About half are ported over to requests, and I'd like to move the other half.

It looks like they are sending this trash for at least 3 years now... :)

> Posted by: Ryan | April 21, 2008 at 01:04 PM
> Yeah, WTH is up with the new Dilbert.com page? Tell whoever it is that runs the server that "text/html; charset=utf-8lias" > is not a valid Content-Type response header.

Taken from http://dilbertblog.typepad.com/the_dilbert_blog/2008/04/apr-for-houses/comments/page/2/

Funny, someone already had a problem with parsing this in Python; see http://objectmix.com/python/784974-where-locate-existing-standard-encodings-python-2.html
We should definitely be catching this.

Not really. `res.content` is no more unicode that's why there's no encoding done when accessing it

``` py
>>> type(requests.get('http://dilbert.com').content)
<type 'str'>
```

However the problem is still present with `res.text` which is unicode

``` py
>>> len(requests.get('http://dilbert.com').text)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
  File "c:\requests\requests\models.py", line 774, in text
    content = str(self.content, encoding, errors='replace')
LookupError: unknown encoding: utf-8lias
```

The error is present regardless of `chardet` module being installed or not.

issue.title: potentially fixes #338

repository.name: requests
repository.description: A simple, yet elegant, HTTP library.

issue.body:
This attempts to fix an issue where encoding of a string might fail when the
encoding is set to some unknown format. Here we attempt to catch the
LookupException and subsequently blindly encode the string one final time.
That is we call str() over response.content without specifying an encoding.
This may still fail in certain cases but does properly handle the case of #338
by returning the expected string.

issue.title: LookupError when you read the text of pages with an unknown encoding

repository.name: requests
repository.description: A simple, yet elegant, HTTP library.

issue.body:
On one of the pages that I'm parsing I got:

  File "/usr/local/lib/python2.7/dist-packages/requests/models.py", line 777, in text
    content = str(self.content, encoding, errors='replace')
  LookupError: unknown encoding: ISO-LATIN-1

I think it would be more sensible to try a default encoding (utf-8 and windows-1252 as a fallback) when Python doesn't support the encoding defined in the page.

Also, using encoding.lower().replace('-latin-', '-8859-') will go a long way fixing the common case of pages using iso-latin-N instead of iso-8859-N.

body: We currently have a pretty robust encoding detection system, but it's only a fallback for when the server doesn't specify an encoding.

We're currently blindly trusting that the encoding that the server is responding with will exist.

Perhaps a map of encodings (e.g. ISO-LATIN-1 => latin1) is best?

> Perhaps a map of encodings (e.g. ISO-LATIN-1 => latin1) is best?

We can't keep adding misspelled and imaginary (ISO-LATIN-1 is not registered alias per http://www.iana.org/assignments/character-sets)  encodings' names found by people on the Internet :)
Providing a hook seems a better approach.

I agree.

You're welcome to do `response.encoding = None`, and it'll use the built-in detection.
so we should make sure that the encoding actually exists in the header detection step
